chunks: 5883 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Wallād al-Ḥannāṭ, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And be good to parents.” What is this iḥsān? So he said:
“Iḥsān is that you keep good companionship with them and that you do not force them to ask you for anything they need, even if they are self-sufficient. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:”
“You will never attain righteousness until you spend out of what you love.”

Then he عليه السلام said: “If one or both of them reach old age with you, then do not say to them ‘uff’” if they irritate you, “and do not rebuke them” if they strike you, “and speak to them a noble word.” The noble word is that you say to them, ‘May Allah forgive you both’; that is a noble word from you. “And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy,” and this means that you do not fill your eyes with staring at them, but look at them with mercy and compassion, and that you do not raise your voice above their voices, nor your hand above their hands, nor go ahead of them.

key_terms.إِحْسَانًا: excellent conduct and goodness in treatment

ai.seo_question: What does the Qur'an mean by showing iḥsān to one's parents?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic command of iḥsān toward parents as gentle companionship, anticipating their needs without making them ask, and maintaining humility and mercy toward them especially in old age. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام interprets the verses by showing that righteousness toward parents is expressed through speech, demeanor, and practical care.
